articles.title: Amazon (AMZN) Faces Earnings Report Amidst Tariff Concerns
articles.summary: Amazon (AMZN) is set to release its first-quarter earnings report on May 1st, amidst concerns over U.S. tariff policies. Analysts are optimistic, with a significant average price target upside of 33.04% to $248.17. This is based on insights from 67 industry analysts, with a high estimate of $295.46 and a low estimate of $195.00. The consensus from 73 brokerage firms is an 'Outperform' status, with an average brokerage recommendation of 1.8. However, GuruFocus estimates the GF Value for Amazon.com Inc (AMZN, Financial) over the next year at $183.63, suggesting a slight downside of 1.56% from its current price.

articles.title: Amazon (AMZN) Price Target Adjusted Amid Tariff Concerns | AMZN
articles.summary: Oppenheimer analyst Jason Helfstein has revised Amazon's (AMZN) price target from $260 to $220 while maintaining an Outperform rating. This adjustment reflects ongoing concerns about the impact of tariffs on e-commerce, particularly on Amazon's financial outlook. According to Helfstein, tariffs will likely burden Amazon's margins rather than its revenues, as the company aims to maintain its market share and customer satisfaction. As investors remain cautious about the effects of tariffs, the focus is on how these factors will influence Amazon's profitability and overall performance.

articles.title: Amazon (AMZN) to Reveal Tariff Impact on Product Prices | AMZN S
articles.summary: Amazon is set to introduce a new feature that will show customers how tariffs contribute to the total cost of products. This change aims to provide buyers with a clearer understanding of how international trade policies affect pricing. Analysts predict an average target price of $246.82, implying an upside of 31.50% from the current price of $187.70. The average brokerage recommendation is 1.8, indicating an 'Outperform' status. GuruFocus estimates the fair value of Amazon to be $183.43, suggesting a downside of 2.27% from the current price.

articles.title: Stock Market Today: S&P posts 6th straight win on talk of tariff relief
articles.summary: The S&P 500 index rose for the sixth straight day, despite two economic reports that suggested consumer unease about the economy. The index was up 20 points at 5,549. Amazon.com (AMZN) had to address a kerfuffle with the White House about displaying tariff costs to customers. However, the company stated that the idea was only considered for its lowest-level priced products and not its main site. The White House responded swiftly, calling the idea a 'hostile and political act.' The Conference Board reported that its Consumer Confidence Index fell to its lowest level since 2020, with 72% of respondents saying a recession in the next 12 months was 'somewhat or very likely.' The S&P CoreLogic reported that home-price growth in the 20 biggest U.S. metropolitan areas is losing steam. The Trump administration has decided to soften the impact of tariffs on domestic and foreign automakers, capping tariffs at 25% for vehicles made outside the U.S. and offering rebates on tariffs for auto parts made outside the U.S. General Motors (GM) pulled its guidance for the year and postponed its analyst call until Thursday, citing tariff uncertainty. Coca-Cola (KO) shares were up premarket after beating earnings estimates, while UPS (UPS) said it was laying off 20,000 workers after curtailing its relationship with Amazon.com (AMZN).

articles.title: Amazon.com Q1 Earnings Preview: All Eyes On E-Commerce Trends, AI As Tariff Anxiety Grows - Amazon.com (NASDAQ:AMZN)
articles.summary: Amazon.com Inc (AMZN) is set to report its first-quarter earnings after market close on Thursday, with analysts expecting revenue of $155.01 billion and earnings per share of $1.36. The company has beaten analyst estimates for revenue in two straight quarters and eight of the last 10 quarters overall. Experts are focused on AI monetization and consumer spending habits, with Freedom Capital Markets Chief Global Strategist Jay Woods saying, 'Investors are also focused on their e-commerce and consumer trends to get a better gauge to see if new spending habits are impacting the bottom line as expectations of tariffs grow.' Analysts will be watching for commentary on tariffs, AI, and cloud, as well as the geographical split of revenue growth and updates on Prime Video subscribers, advertising revenue, and Amazon's new Trainium 2 AI chip.
